Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: Ariba enrollment + PO line-splitting

Hi Dylan,

We're kicking off Ariba enrollment for Redwood as a vendor and hit a mapping question from our procurement systems: NovaMed sometimes issues a single PO that is intentionally split into multiple line items (same PO number, different shipments and GL codes). When we tried to enroll you in Ariba test, the gateway created duplicate PO records on our side and several of our internal downstream systems rejected the acknowledgement.

Attached is a redacted sample (sample_po_1023.xml) and a short screenshot showing the line-splitting behavior. Before we move to full activation we need to confirm:

- Can Redwood accept the same PO number split across multiple line items/shipments under a single acknowledgement?
- If not, what would you need on the Order Form / MSA to make this behavior contractually explicit?

We prefer to avoid a slow legal round if we can add a clarifying clause to the Order Form, but procurement is insisting we get legal alignment. Happy to jump on a short call with your onboarding/tech folks if useful.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Director, Strategic Sourcing
NovaMed Procurement

Two quick clarifying Qs for your team / procurement IT:

Looping in Marissa (legal) for the MSA/order-form question and Tessa (onboarding ops) for the portal mapping work. I've attached a short mapping_notes.csv with possible field mappings that would avoid duplicate records on your side — this is just an initial thought.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: Ariba enrollment + PO line-splitting

Dylan / Tessa — thanks for the context and sample PO. Operationally sounds fine, but contractually we should document how split-line POs are treated to avoid disputes over acceptance and billing. Two points I recommend we add as a short Order Form amendment rather than reopen the full MSA: 

1) PO Aggregation and Acknowledgement: a brief clause that specifies Redwood may acknowledge at the PO-number level or at the individual line level; acceptance occurs when Redwood issues an acknowledgement for the PO or the first accepted line, and such acknowledgement constitutes acceptance for invoicing purposes. This prevents buyers claiming non-acceptance because we acknowledged per PO-number.

2) Split Shipment Invoicing: clarify that multiple invoices referencing the same PO number but different line items/shipments will be accepted and netted against that PO; specify any required reference fields (e.g., PO number + line item id).

Suggested path: I will draft a one-page amendment (Order Form addendum) that both parties can sign — keeps it light and procurement-friendly. Please confirm that NovaMed will accept an Order Form addendum (not a full MSA amendment).

I'll attach the proposed redline for the Order Form addendum and mark the exact clause placement (proposed_amendment_redline.docx). If procurement still insists on MSA-level language we can escalate, but an addendum should be sufficient in ~24-48 hours.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_amendment_redline.docx (docx, 12KB)

Thanks Marissa — procurement is fine with an Order Form addendum. Confirming answers to Dylan's questions:
- We expect a single acknowledgement at the PO-number level where possible; however, our Ariba gateway will sometimes split acknowledgement messages per line during the fulfillment lifecycle. Either is acceptable as long as acknowledgements reference the PO number and line IDs.
- No strict EDI ack window beyond our standard 48-hour acknowledgement SLA.

Attaching the Ariba gateway screenshot and the sample_po_1023.xml again. Procurement IT (proc-it@novamed.com) is happy to join a 20-minute sync if you want to confirm the mapping.

Emily Chen
